blocks.text: AI Won't Replace You
Let's address the fear: AI isn't taking sales jobs. It's making salespeople more effective. That is, AI:

• Handles routine emails and follow-ups
  • Organizes customer data and notes
  • Drafts proposals and presentations
  • Analyzes call patterns and wins
In turn, what only you can do:

• Build genuine relationships
  • Read emotional cues and adapt
  • Negotiate complex deals
  • Close based on trust and rapport
AI is your assistant, not your replacement.
Where Your Time Actually Goes
Track a typical sales day. You'll find hours disappearing into tasks AI can handle faster and better.
Daily Time Drains
Email writing and responses — 2 hours

• Initial outreach emails
  • Follow-up sequences
  • Answering common questions
CRM data entry — 1.5 hours

• Logging calls and meetings
  • Updating deal stages
  • Adding contact notes
Follow-up reminders — 1 hour

• Checking who to contact
  • Remembering context
  • Scheduling next steps
Proposal creation — 1.5 hours

• Customizing templates
  • Finding pricing info
  • Formatting documents
That's 6 hours daily on tasks AI can do in minutes.
Think about it: what could you accomplish with 6 extra hours weekly to actually sell? More discovery calls. Deeper relationship building. Strategic account planning. That's where deals happen.
Real Impact: The Numbers
Sales teams using AI aren't just saving time — they're seeing measurable results. Here's whatAI can help you achieve:

• 6+ hours saved weekly — time you'd spend on emails, data entry, follow-ups
  • Response in minutes, not hours — AI drafts emails instantly
  • No more forgotten follow-ups — AI reminds and drafts your outreach
  • Consistent message quality — every email is well-written, even at 5pm on a Friday
These aren't projections — you'll experience them in the next few lessons.

blocks.question: First, what do you think takes the longest when writing sales emails?

blocks.text: Staring at a blank page, formatting and all other stuff may take more than 2 hours of your day. But what if you could cut that to 20 minutes?
The Email Formula
Great sales emails follow a simple pattern. AI just needs to know four things.
"Write a [tone] email to [person] about [topic] and ask them to [action]" Example: "Write a friendly email to a VP of Sales about saving time on admin work and ask them to schedule a 15-minute call."

blocks.text:
This way, instead of crafting every sentence from scratch, you're giving clear instructions and getting a polished draft back!

You save 10-15 minutes per email. That adds up fast.
Cold Outreach Emails
Let's start with the hardest email: reaching out to someone who doesn't know you yet.

"It's too expensive." "We're already using something else." "Not interested right now." Let's handle objections without sounding defensive or desperate.

So you're actually losing money by not investing—you're paying people to do work a tool can handle. Would it make sense to do a 2-week trial with 5 of your reps? Would you rather contact 200 people who might be interested or 20 who are actively searching for your solution?

• Buy a list of 10,000 contacts
  • Email everyone
  • Hope someone responds
  • 1-2% conversion rate

• Find 20 people showing buying intent
  • Email them with personalized context
  • They're already interested
  • 15-20% conversion rate

Apollo.io is an AI-powered lead finder that searches millions of companies and identifies who's actually interested.

blocks.text: That is, around 80% of sales happen after the 5th contact, but 44% of salespeople give up after just one follow-up. That gap is where deals go to die.
Why Follow-Ups Fail
It's not laziness — it's overwhelm!
What Actually Happens

1. You send a great first email on Monday morning. The prospect doesn't respond.
  2. Tuesday rolls around — should you follow up? Too soon?
  3. By Friday, you're buried in new leads and meetings. That prospect? Forgotten.
  4. Meanwhile, they're buying from your competitor who sent a well-timed follow-up on Wednesday.
You didn't lose because of your product. You lost because of timing.

Think about it: if a prospect showed interest but didn't respond, they're probably just busy — not uninterested.

A well-timed follow-up catches them when they have five minutes. Automation makes sure you're always there at the right moment.
The 3-Email Follow-Up Formula
The most effective follow-up isn't one email. It's a sequence spread over 7 days.

Email 1 (Day 0): Initial outreach
  • Introduce yourself and your value proposition
  • Clear call to action
Email 2 (Day 3): Add value
  • Share a case study, resource, or insight
  • No hard sell, just helpful content
Email 3 (Day 7): Create urgency
  • Time-sensitive offer or question
  • Final clear call to action

  • Tracks everything: who opened, who clicked, who responded
You set it up once. It runs forever.
Setting Up Your First Sequence
Let's walk through creating your automated follow-up in HubSpot.
HubSpot Setup Steps

1. Go to Automation → Workflows in HubSpot.
  2. Create a new workflow and name it (e.g., "Sales Outreach Sequence").
Then, you need to:

1. Add Email 1: paste your ChatGPT email, set to send immediately.
  2. Add Email 2: paste the second email, set the delay to 3 days.
  3. Add Email 3: paste the third email, set the delay to 7 days.
  4. Set enrollment trigger: when a contact fills the form, joins the list, or you manually enroll them.
  5. Activate sequence. Now it runs automatically!

Once activated, every new lead gets the perfect follow-up sequence without you lifting a finger.

You focus on the conversations. HubSpot handles the "checking in."

blocks.text: When Automation Runs vs. When You Step In
Automation isn't about replacing you. It's about freeing you to focus on real conversations.
Let automation handle:

• No response after Email 1 → auto-send Email 2 on Day 3
  • No response after Email 2 → auto-send Email 3 on Day 7
  • Routine "checking in" → consistent touchpoints without manual tracking
  • Initial value delivery → case studies, resources sent automatically
When you step in personally:

• They reply to any email → stop automation, have a real conversation
  • They book a meeting → prepare personally, send confirmation
  • They ask specific questions → answer directly, don't send an automated response
  • High-value accounts → add personal touches throughout sequence
The goal: automation ensures no lead is forgotten, but every conversation feels personal when it matters.

blocks.text: Here's what's really happening: your prospect sees the price, but they haven't fully connected it to the problem it solves or the value it creates. Thus, your job isn't to argue about price. It's to clarify value.
The Five Deadliest Objections

Each one tells you exactly what's missing from your pitch. Let's learn how to respond.
The 3-Part Response Formula
The best objection handlers don't argue or defend. They follow a simple pattern that keeps conversations going.

1. Empathize: acknowledge their concern as valid. "I completely understand budget is a concern..." 2. Reframe: show a different perspective or add context. "...let's look at it as an investment. Your team spends 6 hours weekly on manual work..." 3. Ask a question: uncover the real concern or move forward. "...what would freeing up those hours be worth to your team?" When you argue with an objection, prospects get defensive. When you empathize and explore, they open up.
blocks.title: The Formula:

blocks.text: Handling "It's Too Expensive"
Let's start with the most common objection.

blocks.exampleResponse: Your Response to "It's Too Expensive": "I totally understand—no one wants to spend more than necessary, and budget is always a real consideration. Here's another way to think about it: your team of 15 reps is probably spending about 5 hours each per week on manual follow-ups and data entry. That's 75 hours weekly, or roughly $3,500 in salary paying people to do work our tool automates. Our solution costs $800/month and typically recovers 70% of that time—about 50 hours weekly your team could redirect to selling. So you're actually losing money by not investing. What if we did a 30-day pilot with 5 reps? You'll see exactly how much time they save, and then you can decide if the ROI justifies the cost. Does that sound fair?" Time to prepare: 45 seconds with ChatGPT vs. 10 minutes thinking on your feet

Handling "We Need to Think About It"
This objection is the vaguest — and the most dangerous. It usually means they have concerns they're not sharing.

blocks.exampleResponse: Your Response to "We Need to Think About It": "Absolutely—I wouldn't want you to rush into anything. This is an important decision. Can I ask, when you say you need to think about it, is there a specific aspect you'd like more clarity on? Is it the pricing structure, how implementation would work, or whether the ROI timeline fits your budget cycle? I'm happy to dig into any of those areas right now if that would help—or if there's something else on your mind that I haven't addressed yet?" Follow-up strategy: If they share a concern, address it on the spot. If they're vague, offer a specific resource or comparison.

Handling "We're Already Using Something Else"
Switching costs are real — both financial and psychological. Address both.

blocks.exampleResponse: Your Response to "We're Already Using [Competitor]": "That makes sense—I know [Competitor] is a solid tool, and switching always has a cost in time and training. I'm not here to bash them. Here's what I am curious about, though: what made you take this call if [Competitor] is working well? Usually when people are willing to explore alternatives, there's something they wish worked better. Is it integration challenges? Lack of a feature you need? Or maybe the pricing structure as you've scaled? If we can address that specific gap—and make switching actually worth the transition effort—would it be worth exploring? If not, I totally understand." Key insight: People exploring alternatives usually have a reason. Find it.

blocks.text: Here's what's really happening: your prospect sees the price, but they haven't fully connected it to the problem it solves or the value it creates. Thus, your job isn't to argue about price. It's to clarify value.

Each one tells you exactly what's missing from your pitch. Let's learn how to respond.
The 3-Part Response Formula
The best objection handlers don't argue or defend. They follow a simple pattern that keeps conversations going.

1. Empathize: acknowledge their concern as valid. "I completely understand budget is a concern..." 2. Reframe: show a different perspective or add context. "...let's look at it as an investment. Your team spends 6 hours weekly on manual work..." 3. Ask a question: uncover the real concern or move forward. "...what would freeing up those hours be worth to your team?" When you argue with an objection, prospects get defensive. When you empathize and explore, they open up.

blocks.text: Handling "It's Too Expensive"
Let's start with the most common objection.

blocks.exampleResponse: Your Response to "It's Too Expensive": "I totally understand—no one wants to spend more than necessary, and budget is always a real consideration. Here's another way to think about it: your team of 15 reps is probably spending about 5 hours each per week on manual follow-ups and data entry. That's 75 hours weekly, or roughly $3,500 in salary paying people to do work our tool automates. Our solution costs $800/month and typically recovers 70% of that time—about 50 hours weekly your team could redirect to selling. So you're actually losing money by not investing. What if we did a 30-day pilot with 5 reps? You'll see exactly how much time they save, and then you can decide if the ROI justifies the cost. Does that sound fair?" Time to prepare: 45 seconds with ChatGPT vs. 10 minutes thinking on your feet

Handling "We Need to Think About It"
This objection is the vaguest — and the most dangerous. It usually means they have concerns they're not sharing.

blocks.exampleResponse: Your Response to "We Need to Think About It": "Absolutely—I wouldn't want you to rush into anything. This is an important decision. Can I ask, when you say you need to think about it, is there a specific aspect you'd like more clarity on? Is it the pricing structure, how implementation would work, or whether the ROI timeline fits your budget cycle? I'm happy to dig into any of those areas right now if that would help—or if there's something else on your mind that I haven't addressed yet?" Follow-up strategy: If they share a concern, address it on the spot. If they're vague, offer a specific resource or comparison.

blocks.text:
Here's what happens: you finish a call that didn't go well. You think, "That prospect just wasn't interested."

But what if the real issue was that you talked 80% of the time and never asked about their budget? You'd never know without reviewing the call.
What Call Analysis Reveals
AI doesn't just transcribe your calls — it finds patterns you'd miss even if you listened back.
What AI spots in your calls:

• Talk-to-listen ratio: are you talking too much or listening too little?
  • Questions asked: did you ask enough discovery questions?
  • Keywords mentioned: did you address their pain points?
  • Objections raised: which concerns came up, and how did you handle them?
  • Next steps clarity: did you end with a clear action item?
This is like having a sales coach review every conversation.

For example, AI might reveal that you talk 70% of the time on calls that don't close, but only 40% on calls that do.

That one insight could change your entire approach.
The Golden Ratios
Top-performing salespeople follow patterns. Now you can see if you match them.
What the best reps do:

• Talk-to-listen ratio — 40/60. They listen more than they talk.
  • Questions per call — 8-12. They ask enough to truly understand needs.
  • Customer pain points mentioned — 3-5 times. They reinforce understanding.
  • Next steps confirmed — 100%. Every call ends with a clear action.
  • Objections addressed — within 2 minutes. They don't let concerns linger.
If your numbers are off, you know exactly what to fix.

Think about it: you might feel like you're asking lots of questions, but AI shows you asked 3 when top performers ask 10.

That's actionable feedback you can apply on your very next call.

blocks.question: In your opinion, why do most sales reps struggle to improve their close rate?

blocks.text:
Here's what happens: you finish a call that didn't go well. You think, "That prospect just wasn't interested."

But what if the real issue was that you talked 80% of the time and never asked about their budget? You'd never know without reviewing the call.
What Call Analysis Reveals
AI doesn't just transcribe your calls — it finds patterns you'd miss even if you listened back.
What AI spots in your calls:

• Talk-to-listen ratio: are you talking too much or listening too little?
  • Questions asked: did you ask enough discovery questions?
  • Keywords mentioned: did you address their pain points?
  • Objections raised: which concerns came up, and how did you handle them?
  • Next steps clarity: did you end with a clear action item?
This is like having a sales coach review every conversation.

For example, AI might reveal that you talk 70% of the time on calls that don't close, but only 40% on calls that do.

That one insight could change your entire approach.
The Golden Ratios
Top-performing salespeople follow patterns. Now you can see if you match them.
What the best reps do:

• Talk-to-listen ratio — 40/60. They listen more than they talk.
  • Questions per call — 8-12. They ask enough to truly understand needs.
  • Customer pain points mentioned — 3-5 times. They reinforce understanding.
  • Next steps confirmed — 100%. Every call ends with a clear action.
  • Objections addressed — within 2 minutes. They don't let concerns linger.
If your numbers are off, you know exactly what to fix.

Think about it: you might feel like you're asking lots of questions, but AI shows you asked 3 when top performers ask 10.

That's actionable feedback you can apply on your very next call.
Meet Fireflies.ai
Fireflies.ai joins your calls, records everything, and creates searchable transcripts automatically.
What Fireflies Does

• Auto-joins meetings — add it to your calendar invite, and it shows up
  • Records and transcribes — a full transcript is available 5 minutes after
  • Highlights key moments — action items, questions, objections automatically tagged
  • Analyzes talk time — shows your talk-to-listen ratio
  • Searches across calls — you can find every time you discussed pricing or objections
You never have to take notes during calls again.
Setting Up Call Recording
Let's get Fireflies recording your calls so you have data to analyze.
Fireflies Setup Steps

1. Sign up at Fireflies.ai — free trial covers most needs.
  2. Go to "Integrations" — connect Fireflies to your Google or Microsoft Outlook account.
  3. Add Fireflies to meetings — follow instructions on the Fireflies website.
  4. Fireflies joins automatically — it'll be in the meeting when it starts.
  5. Review transcripts — available in your Fireflies "Meetings" page after the call.

Once set up, Fireflies captures every call automatically. Now you have a library of conversations to learn from.

  • In 6 months, you'll barely recognize your old process.
Final Words

AI doesn't replace your skills — it amplifies them. Your empathy, intuition, and relationship-building? Irreplaceable. AI handles the repetitive work, giving you hours back to focus on what closes deals: human connection.
Start with Week 1. See results. Build momentum. By Week 4, you'll have transformed how you sell! Welcome to the future of sales. You're ready.
